verdict.rationale: LightSprint's own docs describe a managed cloud where you can launch its agents remotely as 'background cloud agents'. Each task gets an isolated sandbox and a branched database when needed, with live previews and 'no local setup needed', so a developer runs agents without operating backend infrastructure. The evidence is marketing-level claims only. missing for 10: technical documentation of the hosted runtime (concurrency/parallelism limits, regions, resource quotas), independent or hands-on corroboration of the managed cloud agents.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use a managed cloud offering to run agents without operating my own backend infrastructure
